content: Sleep eating, also known as Nocturnal Eating Syndrome, is classified as a parasomnia. It is characterized by recurrent episodes of eating during sleep, typically without the individual being aware of their actions. These episodes can occur frequently enough to lead to significant weight gain over time. While sleep eating can affect individuals of all ages and both sexes, it is observed to be more prevalent among young women. In Australia, the medication Ambien, marketed under the name Stilnox, has been associated with side effects such as sleep driving and sleep eating, as reported by the Australian drug regulatory agency. During sleep eating episodes, individuals may repeatedly consume food throughout the night. In some cases, they may eat the same type of food multiple times, often making several trips to the refrigerator or cupboard until the desired food is entirely consumed. Certain medications and alcohol can increase the likelihood of sleepwalking and related behaviors, such as sleep eating, particularly in individuals who are predisposed to these episodes.
